units.text: Overnight mode, the user away while admirals run on standing and night orders.
Load only on the chief of staff's muster or morning-brief announcement, or when the user calls overnight mode.

rules.rule: Overnight mode is loaded only on the chief of staff's muster or morning-brief announcement, or when the user calls overnight mode.

units.text: **Overnight mode** is any long absence of the user.
At **muster**, the chief of staff verifies `overnight: on` with `dydo mode show` before announcing the start; at the **morning brief**, it verifies `overnight: off` before announcing the end.

rules.rule: At muster the chief of staff verifies `overnight: on` with `dydo mode show` before announcing the start; at the morning brief it verifies `overnight: off` before announcing the end.

units.text: In between, **each admiral keeps the conn** of its Project and the chief of staff keeps only the **night watch**.

rules.rule: Between muster and morning brief each admiral keeps the conn of its Project and the chief of staff keeps only the night watch.

units.text: Intent, a watch schedule and message delivery do not establish a mode transition.

rules.rule: Intent, a watch schedule and message delivery do not establish an overnight mode transition; only the verified `dydo mode show` value does.

units.text: Admirals obey the **standing orders** below plus the **night orders**: one Project update per Project, set at muster.

rules.rule: Admirals obey the standing orders plus the night orders: one Project update per Project, set at muster.

units.text: Night orders expire at the morning brief and win where the two conflict.

rules.rule: Night orders expire at the morning brief and win over standing orders where the two conflict.

units.text: The already-invoked chief of staff uses its own resources below.

rules.rule: The already-invoked chief of staff uses its own overnight resources and does not reload its skill.

units.text: Resolve each resource inside the installed `chief-of-staff` skill folder; read it directly without invoking another officer role.

rules.rule: The chief of staff resolves each resource inside the installed `chief-of-staff` skill folder and reads it directly without invoking another officer role.

units.text: While the user is present, complete the [transition preflight](resources/transition-preflight.md) for both startup and shutdown.

rules.rule: While the user is present, the chief of staff completes the transition preflight for both startup and shutdown.

units.text: Record the current mode and prepare the warning/retry and independent readback steps before proceeding.

rules.rule: Before proceeding, record the current mode and prepare the warning/retry and independent readback steps.

units.text: Complete `chief-of-staff`'s `resources/muster.md`.

rules.rule: At startup the chief of staff completes `chief-of-staff`'s `resources/muster.md`.

units.text: Use `grilling` for decisions and `wizard` for terminal steps only.

rules.rule: Muster uses `grilling` for decisions and `wizard` for terminal steps only.

units.text: Proceed once every included admiral confirms its agreed work is runnable and every gap has the user's explicit disposition.

rules.rule: Proceed to activation once every included admiral confirms its agreed work is runnable and every gap has the user's explicit disposition.

units.text: Follow the preflight's warning/retry for `dydo mode set overnight on`.

rules.rule: Follow the preflight's warning/retry for `dydo mode set overnight on`.

units.text: Wait for the setter to return its result, then run `dydo mode show` in a separate later tool call, never in parallel, and require `overnight: on`.

rules.rule: Wait for the mode setter to return its result, then run `dydo mode show` in a separate later tool call, never in parallel, and require the requested value.

units.text: On refusal, failure or missing readback, report activation incomplete with the observed state (unknown if unreadable) and exact recovery action; keep the user present and do not announce activation or say goodnight.

rules.rule: On refusal, failure or missing readback at activation, report activation incomplete with the observed state (unknown if unreadable) and the exact recovery action, keep the user present, and do not announce activation or say goodnight.

units.text: Create the 30-minute watch schedule, returning to this thread.

rules.rule: Create the 30-minute watch schedule, returning to this thread.

units.text: Preserve the complete schedule ID exactly as returned by the host, including any prefix, for deletion at shutdown.

rules.rule: Preserve the complete schedule ID exactly as the host returns it, including any prefix, for deletion at shutdown.

units.text: If scheduling fails, report mode on with watch unavailable and resolve it while the user is present.

rules.rule: If scheduling fails, report mode on with watch unavailable and resolve it while the user is present.

units.text: Announce the verified start to every included admiral.

rules.rule: Announce the verified start to every included admiral.

units.text: Done when readiness is confirmed, the schedule ID is preserved, mode is on and every included admiral has the announcement.

rules.rule: Startup is done when readiness is confirmed, the schedule ID is preserved, mode is on and every included admiral has the announcement.

units.text: **Keep the conn.**
Project decisions are the admiral's.

rules.rule: Project decisions are the admiral's overnight.

units.text: **Decide by weight.**
Easily reversible: decide and record `DECIDED`.

rules.rule: An easily reversible overnight call is decided by the admiral and recorded `DECIDED`.

units.text: Other calls: `what-would-balazs-do`, whose trigger map decides it or prepares the Question; irreversible calls are always a Question.

rules.rule: Other overnight calls go to `what-would-balazs-do`, whose trigger map decides it or prepares the Question; irreversible calls are always a Question.

units.text: **Merge into the feature branch** through your captain's Merge chain, which runs `dydo merge`; never into master or main.

rules.rule: Overnight merges go into the feature branch through the captain's Merge chain, which runs `dydo merge`; never into master or main.

units.text: **The board is the report.**
Send the chief of staff no status.

rules.rule: Admirals send the chief of staff no status overnight.

units.text: Contact it for cross-Project trouble: collisions, shared-resource problems, and heads-ups or permission before actions that affect other agents.

rules.rule: Admirals contact the chief of staff for cross-Project trouble: collisions, shared-resource problems, and heads-ups or permission before actions that affect other agents.

units.text: It relays down admiral → captain → crew.

rules.rule: The chief of staff relays down the chain admiral to captain to crew.

units.text: Answer a nudge in one line.

rules.rule: Answer a chief-of-staff nudge in one line.

units.text: **Keep moving.**
One blocker never stops the night: take the next pickable work.

rules.rule: One blocker never stops the night: take the next pickable work.

units.text: Stop only at the night orders' stop line or when nothing is pickable.

rules.rule: Stop only at the night orders' stop line or when nothing is pickable.

units.text: The walking skeleton does not wait either: its Walkthrough Ticket blocks nothing; post `DECIDED` on it, carry on, and treat a wrong direction as a revert.

rules.rule: The walking skeleton does not wait overnight: its Walkthrough Ticket blocks nothing; post `DECIDED` on it, carry on, and treat a wrong direction as a revert.

units.text: **Write for a reader who wasn't there**, every Question and `DECIDED`.

rules.rule: Write every Question and `DECIDED` for a reader who wasn't there.

units.text: Withdraw only Questions made obsolete by discovered facts or completed work; keep tribunal-decided Questions awaiting ratification.

rules.rule: Withdraw only Questions made obsolete by discovered facts or completed work; keep tribunal-decided Questions awaiting ratification.

units.text: The chief of staff runs its Overnight duties watch step every 30 minutes, using its `resources/night-survey.md`.

rules.rule: The chief of staff runs its Overnight duties watch step every 30 minutes, using its `resources/night-survey.md`.

units.text: The surveyor inspects; the chief of staff acts on its findings:

rules.rule: The surveyor inspects; the chief of staff acts on its findings.

units.text: Idle, or waiting with nothing in flight and runnable work: send one specific nudge naming the evidence.

rules.rule: For an idle admiral, or one waiting with nothing in flight and runnable work, send one specific nudge naming the evidence.

units.text: Nudge unanswered: inspect the relevant captain threads and intervene with the owner.

rules.rule: When a nudge goes unanswered, inspect the relevant captain threads and intervene with the owner.

units.text: The board and threads carry state; never ask for routine STATE.

rules.rule: The board and threads carry state; never ask for routine STATE.

units.text: Mediate cross-Project trouble by chief-of-staff Method step 4, Mediate a collision, relaying heads-ups down the chain.

rules.rule: Mediate cross-Project trouble by chief-of-staff Method step 4, Mediate a collision, relaying heads-ups down the chain.

units.text: After any gap in the watch, rebuild from Linear and sweep everyone by Method step 5, Sweep the board.

rules.rule: After any gap in the watch, rebuild from Linear and sweep everyone by Method step 5, Sweep the board.

units.text: When the user says he's back, in the chief of staff's conversation:

rules.rule: When the user says he's back, shutdown runs in the chief of staff's conversation.

units.text: Complete the [transition preflight](resources/transition-preflight.md) for shutdown while the user is present; record the current mode before changing it.

rules.rule: Complete the transition preflight for shutdown while the user is present, recording the current mode before changing it.

units.text: Delete the watch schedule using the complete preserved ID.

rules.rule: Delete the watch schedule using the complete preserved ID.

units.text: List schedules and confirm that exact ID is absent before claiming the watch stopped; report a deletion or verification gap.

rules.rule: List schedules and confirm that exact ID is absent before claiming the watch stopped; report a deletion or verification gap.

units.text: Settle any pending survey through its host lifecycle so no tick remains in flight.

rules.rule: Settle any pending survey through its host lifecycle so no tick remains in flight.

units.text: Follow the preflight's warning/retry for `dydo mode set overnight off`.

rules.rule: Follow the preflight's warning/retry for `dydo mode set overnight off`.

units.text: Wait for the setter to return its result, then run `dydo mode show` in a separate later tool call, never in parallel, and require `overnight: off`, then announce the end to every included admiral.

rules.rule: Wait for the setter to return, then run `dydo mode show` in a separate later call and require `overnight: off`, then announce the end to every included admiral.

units.text: On refusal, failure or missing readback, report shutdown incomplete with the observed state (unknown if unreadable) and exact recovery action.

rules.rule: On refusal, failure or missing readback at shutdown, report shutdown incomplete with the observed state (unknown if unreadable) and the exact recovery action.

units.text: A deleted schedule does not prove mode is off.

rules.rule: A deleted schedule does not prove mode is off.

units.text: Fill `chief-of-staff`'s `resources/morning-brief.md` in the conversation, writing nothing to the repo.

rules.rule: Fill `chief-of-staff`'s `resources/morning-brief.md` in the conversation, writing nothing to the repo.

units.text: Use `wizard` for terminal unblockers only.

rules.rule: The morning brief uses `wizard` for terminal unblockers only.

units.text: Done when the schedule is confirmed absent, pending surveys are settled, mode is off, admirals have the announcement and the user has the brief.

rules.rule: Shutdown is done when the schedule is confirmed absent, pending surveys are settled, mode is off, admirals have the announcement and the user has the brief.

units.text: The already-invoked chief of staff prepares startup and shutdown while the user is present.

rules.rule: The already-invoked chief of staff prepares startup and shutdown while the user is present.

units.text: Read `dydo mode show` and record the observed value.

rules.rule: Read `dydo mode show` and record the observed value.

units.text: Confirm the agreed work and stop line before activation.

rules.rule: Confirm the agreed work and stop line before activation.

units.text: The transition commands are:

```text
Start: dydo mode set overnight on
End:   dydo mode set overnight off
```

rules.rule: The transition commands are `dydo mode set overnight on` to start and `dydo mode set overnight off` to end.

units.text: Run the applicable command only as the chief of staff readying overnight mode or ending it; otherwise stop.

rules.rule: Run the transition command only as the chief of staff readying overnight mode or ending it; otherwise stop.

units.text: On Claude, Codex, T3 and direct guard invocation, the guard stops an attempt with that reminder unless a pass-through marker is already armed.
If the reminder applies to you, retry the same command once.

rules.rule: If the guard's reminder applies to you, retry the same command once.

units.text: Markers are global and have no expiry: an earlier caller may have armed the same command, so your next attempt may pass immediately.
The guard keys the warning by the full command with whitespace runs normalized.
A different command, including the opposite transition, receives its own warning.
The retry passes the warning; ordinary hard blocks still apply on every attempt.
This nudge prevents accidents.
It does not authenticate your role or prove human approval.
Wait for `dydo mode set` to return its result.

rules.rule: Wait for `dydo mode set` to return its result, then run `dydo mode show` in a separate later tool call, never in parallel with the setter.

units.text: Only then run `dydo mode show` in a separate later tool call, never in parallel with the setter.
Require the requested value before announcing activation or shutdown.

rules.rule: Require the requested mode value in the readback before announcing activation or shutdown.

units.text: A warning, retry, successful setter exit, schedule or message establishes no transition by itself.

rules.rule: A warning, retry, successful setter exit, schedule or message establishes no transition by itself.

units.text: Capture the action, result and fresh readback separately.

rules.rule: Capture the action, the result and the fresh readback separately.

units.text: If the value already matched before execution, report it as already on/off rather than claiming a new transition.

rules.rule: If the value already matched before execution, report it as already on/off rather than claiming a new transition.

units.text: On any unexpected refusal, execution failure, missing readback or mismatched value, report the transition incomplete with the actual result and current observed state; if the readback failed, say the state is unknown.

rules.rule: On any unexpected refusal, execution failure, missing readback or mismatched value, report the transition incomplete with the actual result and current observed state; if the readback failed, say the state is unknown.

units.text: Preserve the existing state and evidence.

rules.rule: On a failed transition, preserve the existing state and evidence.

units.text: Return the blocker to the responsible captain or user with the exact action needed.

rules.rule: Return the blocker to the responsible captain or user with the exact action needed.

units.text: Use `wizard` for terminal help when needed.

rules.rule: Use `wizard` for terminal help when needed.

units.text: Resolve the blocker before proceeding; every recovery still needs fresh readback.

rules.rule: Resolve the blocker before proceeding; every recovery still needs fresh readback.

units.text: Show me the product as it stands - what changed since the last walkthrough, where to look first, and how to try it.
Load only when the user asks, or at the map holder's Milestone or landing step.

rules.rule: Load the walkthrough skill only when the user asks, or at the map holder's Milestone or landing step.

units.text: Give the user the tour of the whole product as it stands, so it makes sense to him even when he is not close in.

rules.rule: Give the user a tour of the whole product as it stands, so it makes sense to him even when he is not close in.

units.text: A Project has one Walkthrough Ticket per Milestone, the landing's last.

rules.rule: A Project has one Walkthrough Ticket per Milestone, the landing's last.

units.text: At a Milestone, walk the feature branch at the SHA its last merge left; at the landing, walk main after it landed.

rules.rule: At a Milestone walk the feature branch at the SHA its last merge left; at the landing walk main after it landed.

units.text: The map holder runs the ticket with the user; he walks it, or skips it, and a skip is his verdict to go on.

rules.rule: The map holder runs the Walkthrough Ticket with the user; the user walks it or skips it, and a skip is his verdict to go on.

units.text: The argument names what to walk - a Milestone, a Project's landing, a feature branch, a ticket, a diff range.
Ask which one when it is missing.

rules.rule: Ask which target to walk when the argument is missing.

units.text: Walk it yourself first: the whole state at that SHA, the diff since the last walkthrough and its hops, the tickets it closed with their review blocks, the DRs and applicable spec sections those tickets cite, the returns their crew posted.

rules.rule: Walk the target yourself first: the whole state at that SHA, the diff since the last walkthrough and its hops, the closed tickets with their review blocks, the DRs and spec sections they cite, and the returns their crew posted.

units.text: Then brief the user in four parts, the newest changes first, and mark the ones that need his careful look: where a drift from his intent would cost most, or a review left doubt.

rules.rule: Brief the user in four parts, newest changes first, marking the ones that need his careful look: where a drift from his intent would cost most, or a review left doubt.

units.text: **What changed and why** - the current state in one paragraph, then what changed since the last walkthrough, each part traced to the ticket that carried it and the DR that decided it, with the shape drawn by `show-me` where a tree or a diff says it faster than prose.

rules.rule: Part one, What changed and why: the current state in one paragraph, then what changed since the last walkthrough, each part traced to its ticket and DR, with the shape drawn by `show-me` where a tree or diff says it faster than prose.

units.text: **Where to look first** - a route for his own file-by-file pass: the parts marked for a careful look, the files that drew findings, then the ones a crew member left an open doubt on, then the seams the change moved.

rules.rule: Part two, Where to look first: a route for his file-by-file pass: the parts marked for careful look, the files that drew findings, the files a crew member left an open doubt on, then the seams the change moved.

units.text: **How to try it** - the exact commands to build it and see the new behaviour, in order, each one run once by you so it is true when he types it.

rules.rule: Part three, How to try it: the exact commands to build it and see the new behaviour, in order, each run once by you so it is true when he types it.

units.text: **What reviewers flagged or deferred** - in the severities the **Severity** entry of `dydo/reference/dydo-glossary.md` defines: each `should` deferred and the ticket where it now lives, reported as it stands.

rules.rule: Part four, What reviewers flagged or deferred: in the glossary's Severity terms, each `should` deferred and the ticket where it now lives, reported as it stands.

units.text: At the landing, also every unaddressed `nit` with the ticket record where it sits, and every open inquisition nit ticket, for the user to promote any.

rules.rule: At the landing, also report every unaddressed `nit` with the ticket record where it sits, and every open inquisition nit ticket, for the user to promote any.

units.text: The tour ends when the user has inspected the files and tried the behavior, or skipped it.

rules.rule: The tour ends when the user has inspected the files and tried the behavior, or skipped it.

units.text: Record his verdict on the Walkthrough Ticket in his own words, or the skip.

rules.rule: Record the user's verdict on the Walkthrough Ticket in his own words, or the skip.

units.text: Other tours route findings through ordinary tickets.

rules.rule: Other (non-Milestone, non-landing) tours route findings through ordinary tickets.

units.text: A Milestone's findings become tickets in the same Project as they arrive.

rules.rule: A Milestone's findings become tickets in the same Project as they arrive.

units.text: At the landing, record findings as tickets in the same Project; the map holder commissions the first fix Captain to re-cut its feature branch from main for fixes and another landing/walkthrough.

rules.rule: At the landing, record findings as tickets in the same Project; the map holder commissions the first fix Captain to re-cut its feature branch from main for fixes and another landing/walkthrough.

units.text: An empty landing walkthrough lets the Project close; the map holder commissions spec retirement following `dydo/reference/feature-spec-convention.md`, read from the repository root.

rules.rule: An empty landing walkthrough lets the Project close; the map holder commissions spec retirement following `dydo/reference/feature-spec-convention.md`, read from the repository root.

units.text: Keep the brief in the terminal, or in a scratch file when the user wants to read it beside the diff.

rules.rule: Keep the brief in the terminal, or in a scratch file when the user wants to read it beside the diff.

units.text: The durable record stays where it already is: the tickets, the review blocks and the DRs the tour points at.

rules.rule: The durable record stays where it already is: the tickets, review blocks and DRs the tour points at.

units.text: Fog in a Project map or inside one ticket.
Chart the visible route as Wayfinding Tickets and resolve them one at a time until the destination is reached.

rules.rule: Chart the visible route as Wayfinding Tickets and resolve them one at a time until the destination is reached.

units.text: The destination is known, but the route is wrapped in **fog**.
Wayfinding finds that route; it does not charge at the destination.

rules.rule: Wayfinding finds the route to the destination; it does not charge at the destination.

units.text: The map holds the low-resolution view, and its **Wayfinding Tickets** clear one part of the route at a time.
The **map holder** charts and grills.

rules.rule: The map holder charts and grills.

units.text: A Project's map holder is the user, driving the map in his own session, or an admiral the user invoked, until the user takes the map back; the Project description names the current holder.

rules.rule: A Project's map holder is the user, driving the map in his own session, or an admiral the user invoked, until the user takes the map back; the Project description names the current holder.

units.text: A Ticket Captain may chart local fog inside one approved delivery outcome.

rules.rule: A Ticket Captain may chart local fog inside one approved delivery outcome.

units.text: For a communication protocol, from the repository root read only the Communication and evidence section in `dydo/reference/linear-workspace-standard.md`, not the whole workspace standard.

rules.rule: For a communication protocol, read only the Communication and evidence section of `dydo/reference/linear-workspace-standard.md` from the repository root, not the whole standard.

units.text: Wayfinder advances large work one manageable step at a time.
Ticket Captains deliver clear Tasks; Wayfinding Tickets clear the fog blocking what comes next.

rules.rule: Ticket Captains deliver clear Tasks; Wayfinding Tickets clear the fog blocking what comes next.

units.text: Defer later decisions until delivery reveals the facts they need.

rules.rule: Defer later decisions until delivery reveals the facts they need.

units.text: The map is complete at the destination, with no open Tasks or unresolved fog.

rules.rule: The map is complete at the destination, with no open Tasks or unresolved fog.

units.text: In everything the user reads, name every Project and ticket by its title, with its Linear key and URL inside that name.

rules.rule: In everything the user reads, name every Project and ticket by its title, with its Linear key and URL inside that name.

units.text: Titles scan; walls of bare keys do not.
At Project scale, the Linear Project description is the whole map at low resolution.

rules.rule: At Project scale, the Linear Project description is the whole map at low resolution.

units.text: It indexes; each Wayfinding Ticket stores its own context and resolution.

rules.rule: The map indexes; each Wayfinding Ticket stores its own context and resolution.

units.text: Link shared feature anchors following `dydo/reference/feature-spec-convention.md`, read from the repository root when creating or changing one.

rules.rule: Link shared feature anchors following `dydo/reference/feature-spec-convention.md`, read from the repository root when creating or changing one.

units.text: Open tickets are found through Linear queries.

rules.rule: Open tickets are found through Linear queries, not listed in the map.

units.text:
```markdown
**Map holder:** <the user, or the admiral the user invoked; rewritten when the map changes hands>

## Destination

<what will exist or work differently when this Project is complete; one or two lines>

## Notes

<domain, methods each session should reach for, standing preferences>

## Resolutions so far

- [<closed ticket title and key>](Linear URL): <one-line gist of the resolution>

## Not yet specified

<!-- see "Fog of war": in-scope fog you can't create a ticket for yet; graduates as the frontier advances -->

## Out of scope

<!-- see "Out of scope": work ruled beyond the destination; closed, never graduates -->
```

rules.rule: The Project map description has this form: Map holder line, Destination, Notes, Resolutions so far, Not yet specified, Out of scope.

units.text: At delivery scale, the parent Task is the local map; the Project's map holder should already have cleared most of its fog.

rules.rule: At delivery scale the parent Task is the local map; the Project's map holder should already have cleared most of its fog.

units.text: If delivery reveals more, the Captain creates a direct Wayfinding Sub-ticket and records its resolution on it.

rules.rule: If delivery reveals more fog, the Captain creates a direct Wayfinding Sub-ticket and records its resolution on it.

units.text: Anything that could affect another ticket, a shared contract, or the Project map is escalated to the Project's map holder instead.

rules.rule: Anything that could affect another ticket, a shared contract, or the Project map is escalated to the Project's map holder instead of resolved locally.

units.text: The map contains both Tasks and Wayfinding Tickets.
Tasks are the route someone builds; a Ticket Captain owns each one end to end.

rules.rule: Tasks are the route someone builds; a Ticket Captain owns each one end to end.

units.text: Wayfinding Tickets clear the fog around that route.
Each ticket has a name, Linear key, and URL.

rules.rule: Each ticket has a name, Linear key, and URL.

units.text: Its body carries one outcome sized to one agent session.

rules.rule: A ticket's body carries one outcome sized to one agent session.

units.text: Assignment is the claim: assign it first, before any work, so concurrent sessions skip it.

rules.rule: Assignment is the claim: assign the ticket first, before any work, so concurrent sessions skip it.

units.text: Blocking uses Linear's native dependency relationship: essential because it renders the frontier visually in Linear, so the user sees what is takeable without opening the map.

rules.rule: Blocking uses Linear's native dependency relationship, so the frontier renders visually in Linear.

units.text: A ticket is **unblocked** when every ticket blocking it is closed; the **frontier** is the open, unblocked, unassigned tickets at the edge of the known.
The resolution is recorded as a named evidence comment using the `DECIDED` form in the communication protocol.

rules.rule: A Wayfinding Ticket's resolution is recorded as a named evidence comment using the `DECIDED` form in the communication protocol.

units.text: Assets created while resolving a ticket are linked from it, not pasted in.

rules.rule: Assets created while resolving a ticket are linked from it, not pasted in.

units.text: For the Project's map holder, contracts are tickets under the Project; for a captain they are Sub-tickets under its ticket.

rules.rule: For the Project's map holder, contracts are tickets under the Project; for a captain they are Sub-tickets under its ticket.

units.text: The same Types, statuses and chain hold.

rules.rule: The same Types, statuses and chain hold for Project-level and delivery-level contracts.

units.text: The captain specifies its parent before naming disjoint parallel lanes, and each merging lane or ticket gets its own Merge Sub-ticket in order, except an atomic ticket's own merge into main.

rules.rule: The captain specifies its parent before naming disjoint parallel lanes, and each merging lane or ticket gets its own Merge Sub-ticket in order, except an atomic ticket's own merge into main.

units.text: The standard owns the full Type set and status/priority rules: from the repository root, read `dydo/reference/linear-workspace-standard.md`.

rules.rule: The standard owns the full Type set and status/priority rules: read `dydo/reference/linear-workspace-standard.md` from the repository root.

units.text: Every captain-held ticket carries Mode **HITL** (human in the loop, worked _with_ a human who speaks for themselves) or **AFK**, driven by the agent alone.

rules.rule: Every captain-held ticket carries Mode HITL (worked with a human who speaks for themselves) or AFK (driven by the agent alone).

units.text: A HITL ticket only resolves through that live exchange; the agent never stands in for the user's side of it (a grilling agent that answers its own questions has broken this).

rules.rule: A HITL ticket resolves only through the live exchange with the user; the agent never stands in for the user's side of it.

units.text: **Task** (HITL or AFK): the role a captain-held ticket plays on the map, as the standard defines it.
Its Ticket Captain and crew carry it through its contract, production, review, and its Merge Sub-ticket.

rules.rule: A Task's Ticket Captain and crew carry it through its contract, production, review, and its Merge Sub-ticket.

units.text: **Research**: Reading documentation, third-party APIs, or local resources like knowledge bases to surface a fact a decision waits on.
Resolved by a subagent that calls the Skill tool with "research".

rules.rule: A Research Ticket is resolved by a subagent that calls the Skill tool with "research".

units.text: Use when authoritative evidence, inside or outside the repository, can settle the fact.

rules.rule: Use Research when authoritative evidence, inside or outside the repository, can settle the fact.

units.text: **Prototype** (HITL): Raise the fidelity of the discussion by making a cheap, rough, concrete artifact to react to (throwaway UI or logic code) by calling the Skill tool with "prototype".

rules.rule: A Prototype ticket (HITL) makes a cheap, rough, concrete artifact to react to by calling the Skill tool with "prototype".

units.text: Links the prototype as an asset.

rules.rule: A Prototype ticket links the prototype as an asset.

units.text: Use when "how should it look" or "how should it behave" is the key question.

rules.rule: Use Prototype when "how should it look" or "how should it behave" is the key question.

units.text: **Grilling**: Conversation.
The default case.

rules.rule: Grilling is the default Wayfinding Ticket type.

units.text: Always call the Skill tool twice, for "grilling" and "domain-modeling".

rules.rule: A Grilling ticket always calls the Skill tool twice, for "grilling" and "domain-modeling".

units.text: **Question**: One prepared human choice that authoritative sources and the other ticket types cannot settle.
The ticket carries the homework, credible options, trade-offs, and recommendation.

rules.rule: A Question ticket carries the homework, credible options, trade-offs, and recommendation.

units.text: **Enablement** (HITL or AFK): the access, environment, credentials or material other work needs, as the standard defines it: nothing to decide, prototype, or research, but the work is blocked until it is done.
Signing up for a service so its API can be judged, provisioning access, moving data so its shape can be seen.
This is the one Wayfinding type that _does_ rather than decides.

notRule.note: Enablement is the one type that does rather than decides

units.text: A captain drives Enablement alone where it can (AFK); for human-only steps it uses `wizard` in a top-level HITL session.

rules.rule: A captain drives Enablement alone where it can (AFK); for human-only steps it uses `wizard` in a top-level HITL session.

units.text: Prototype also has a captain; Research, Grilling and Question stay with the map holder.

rules.rule: Prototype also has a captain; Research, Grilling and Question stay with the map holder.

units.text: Resolved when the work is done; the answer records what was done and any resulting facts (credentials location, new URLs, row counts) later tickets depend on.

rules.rule: Enablement is resolved when the work is done; the answer records what was done and any resulting facts later tickets depend on.

units.text: The map is _deliberately_ incomplete: don't chart what you can't yet see.

rules.rule: The map is deliberately incomplete: do not chart what you cannot yet see.

units.text: Beyond the live tickets lies the **fog of war**: the dim view of decisions and investigations you can tell are coming but can't yet pin down, because they hang on questions still open.
Resolving a ticket clears the fog ahead of it, graduating whatever's now specifiable into fresh tickets, one at a time, until the way to the destination is clear and no tickets remain.

rules.rule: Resolving a ticket clears the fog ahead of it, graduating whatever is now specifiable into fresh tickets, one at a time, until the way is clear and no tickets remain.

units.text: The map's **Not yet specified** section is where that dim view is written down: the suspected question, the area to revisit later.

rules.rule: The map's Not yet specified section is where the dim view is written down: the suspected question, the area to revisit later.

units.text: It's the undiscovered frontier _toward_ the destination: everything here is in scope, just not sharp enough to become a ticket.
Write as loosely or as fully as the view allows; it doubles as a signpost for collaborators reading where the effort is headed.

rules.rule: Write Not yet specified as loosely or as fully as the view allows.

units.text: **Fog or ticket?**
The test is whether you can state the question precisely now, _not_ whether you can answer it now.

rules.rule: Fog or ticket is decided by whether you can state the question precisely now, not whether you can answer it now.

units.text: **Ticket when** the question is already sharp, even if it's blocked and you can't act on it yet.

rules.rule: Make it a ticket when the question is already sharp, even if blocked.

units.text: **Not yet specified when** you can't yet phrase it that sharply.

rules.rule: Put it in Not yet specified when you cannot yet phrase the question that sharply.

units.text: Don't pre-slice the fog into ticket-sized pieces: it's coarser than a ticket, and one patch may graduate into several tickets, or none, once the frontier reaches it.

rules.rule: Do not pre-slice the fog into ticket-sized pieces.

units.text: **Not yet specified** excludes what is already resolved (Resolutions so far), what is already a live ticket, and what is out of scope.

rules.rule: Not yet specified excludes what is already resolved, what is already a live ticket, and what is out of scope.

units.text: Search the governing Decision Records, Project plan, specifications, documentation, standards, code, tests, and prior answers first.

rules.rule: Before creating a Question, search the governing Decision Records, Project plan, specifications, documentation, standards, code, tests, and prior answers first.

units.text: Use Research, Prototype, Grilling, or Enablement where they can clear the fog.

rules.rule: Use Research, Prototype, Grilling, or Enablement where they can clear the fog.

units.text: `Question` is the last rung: create it only when human judgment still remains.

rules.rule: Question is the last rung: create it only when human judgment still remains.

units.text: Fog can surface through several hands:
| Project's map holder | create and wire it while charting, or as delivery clears Project fog |

rules.rule: The Project's map holder creates and wires a fog ticket while charting, or as delivery clears Project fog.

units.text: | Code Writer or other crew | return a prepared hand-raise to the Ticket Captain |

rules.rule: Code Writer or other crew return a prepared hand-raise to the Ticket Captain.

units.text: | Ticket Captain | create a local Sub-ticket, or escalate a Project-level packet to the Project's map holder |

rules.rule: A Ticket Captain creates a local Sub-ticket, or escalates a Project-level packet to the Project's map holder.

units.text: An answer graduates to a Decision Record only when it is hard to reverse, surprising later, and the result of a real trade-off.

rules.rule: An answer graduates to a Decision Record only when it is hard to reverse, surprising later, and the result of a real trade-off.

units.text: The ticket carries the question and its working resolution; the Decision Record carries the durable decision.

rules.rule: The ticket carries the question and its working resolution; the Decision Record carries the durable decision.

units.text: Link them rather than copying them.

rules.rule: Link the ticket and the Decision Record rather than copying one into the other.

units.text: Fog only ever gathers _toward_ the destination.
The destination fixes the scope, so work beyond it is **out of scope**: it isn't fog, and it doesn't belong in **Not yet specified**.

rules.rule: Work beyond the destination is out of scope: it is not fog and does not belong in Not yet specified.

units.text: It gets its own **Out of scope** section on the map: work you've consciously ruled out of _this_ effort.

rules.rule: Out-of-scope work gets its own Out of scope section on the map.

units.text: Scope, not sharpness, lands it here.

rules.rule: Scope, not sharpness, puts work in Out of scope.

units.text: Out-of-scope work never graduates (the frontier stops at the destination), so it returns only if the destination is redrawn, and then as a fresh effort, not a resumption.

rules.rule: Out-of-scope work never graduates; it returns only if the destination is redrawn, and then as a fresh effort.

units.text: Ruling something out of scope is a scoping act, not a step on the route.

notRule.note: ruling out is a scoping act

units.text: When a ticket that already exists turns out to sit past the destination (mis-scoped while charting, or exposed by a resolution), mark it `Canceled` and leave one line in the **Out of scope** section: the gist plus why it's out of scope, linking the ticket.

rules.rule: When an existing ticket turns out to sit past the destination, mark it `Canceled` and leave one line in Out of scope: the gist plus why it is out of scope, linking the ticket.

units.text: It stays out of **Resolutions so far**, which records the route actually walked; a scope boundary isn't a step on it.

rules.rule: Out-of-scope entries stay out of Resolutions so far, which records only the route actually walked.

units.text: Two modes.
Either way, a session the user drives never resolves more than one Wayfinding Ticket, with the exception of Research Tickets: one ticket is sized to one session.

rules.rule: A session the user drives never resolves more than one Wayfinding Ticket, except Research Tickets.

units.text: An invoked admiral is exempt.

rules.rule: An invoked admiral is exempt from the one-ticket-per-session limit.

units.text: Tasks may run concurrently under separate Ticket Captains.

rules.rule: Tasks may run concurrently under separate Ticket Captains.

units.text: Charting starts from a Linear Project and a loose destination.
**Name the destination.**
Use `grilling` and `domain-modeling` to pin down what this map is finding its way to: the spec, Decision Record, or change.

rules.rule: Use `grilling` and `domain-modeling` to pin down what the map is finding its way to: the spec, Decision Record, or change.

units.text: The destination fixes the scope, so it is settled first.

rules.rule: Settle the destination first, since it fixes the scope.

units.text: **Map the frontier.**
Grill again, **breadth-first** this time: fan out across the whole space rather than deep on any one thread, surfacing the open questions and the first steps takeable now.

rules.rule: Grill again breadth-first: fan out across the whole space rather than deep on one thread, surfacing the open questions and the first steps takeable now.

units.text: **If this surfaces no fog** (the way to the destination is already clear, the whole journey small enough for one session), no map is needed.

rules.rule: If charting surfaces no fog (the way is clear and the whole journey fits one session), no map is needed.

units.text: **Write the map:** Destination and Notes filled in, Resolutions so far empty, the fog sketched into **Not yet specified**.

rules.rule: Write the map: Destination and Notes filled in, Resolutions so far empty, the fog sketched into Not yet specified.

units.text: In a Project an admiral scaffolds, its scaffold recipe commits the Project's spec; this step covers feature specs inside it.

rules.rule: In a Project an admiral scaffolds, its scaffold recipe commits the Project's spec; the map-writing step covers feature specs inside it.

units.text: For shared behavior or decisions needing one current anchor, choose an applicable reviewed architecture plan or feature spec, creating a spec where needed under `dydo/reference/feature-spec-convention.md`.

rules.rule: For shared behavior or decisions needing one current anchor, choose an applicable reviewed architecture plan or feature spec, creating a spec where needed under `dydo/reference/feature-spec-convention.md`.

units.text: Commit a new spec under the map holder's custody and make that commit reachable to recipients before relying on its Project-map link; otherwise record the anchor as unresolved.

rules.rule: Commit a new spec under the map holder's custody and make that commit reachable to recipients before relying on its Project-map link; otherwise record the anchor as unresolved.

units.text: Atomic intent stays in its ticket.

rules.rule: Atomic intent stays in its ticket, not in a spec anchor.

units.text: **Create the tickets you can specify now**, both Tasks and Wayfinding Tickets, then wire blocking edges in a **second pass** (tickets need keys before they can reference each other).

rules.rule: Create the tickets you can specify now, both Tasks and Wayfinding Tickets, then wire blocking edges in a second pass.

units.text: Derive affected Tasks from the anchor's relevant sections and link those sections in their bounded contracts.

rules.rule: Derive affected Tasks from the anchor's relevant sections and link those sections in their bounded contracts.

units.text: Wiring sorts them into the frontier and the blocked; everything you cannot yet specify stays in the fog.
At Project scale, group the Tasks into the Project's Milestones in Linear: few and meaningful, the walking skeleton first, the landing last.

rules.rule: At Project scale, group the Tasks into the Project's Milestones in Linear: few and meaningful, the walking skeleton first, the landing last.

units.text: **Fire the Research subagents.**

For each Research Ticket just created that is unassigned, in `Todo` and unblocked, claim it, then spin up a subagent that uses `research` to resolve it in parallel, recording its cited findings as a comment on that ticket.

rules.rule: For each Research Ticket just created that is unassigned, in `Todo` and unblocked, claim it, then spin up a subagent that uses `research` to resolve it in parallel, recording its cited findings as a comment on that ticket.

units.text: Stop: charting is one session's work; it resolves nothing itself.

rules.rule: Charting is one session's work and resolves nothing itself; stop after firing the Research subagents.

units.text: Working starts from a Project or parent delivery ticket.

rules.rule: Working starts from a Project or parent delivery ticket.

units.text: Naming a frontier ticket is optional: without one, take the next ticket rather than asking the user to choose.

rules.rule: Naming a frontier ticket is optional: without one, take the next ticket rather than asking the user to choose.

units.text: Load the **map**: the low-resolution view, not every ticket body.

rules.rule: Load the map, the low-resolution view, not every ticket body.

units.text: Choose the ticket.
If one was named, use it.

rules.rule: If a ticket was named, use it.

units.text: Otherwise take the first pickable frontier ticket in `Todo`.

rules.rule: Otherwise take the first pickable frontier ticket in `Todo`.

units.text: A captain-held Type goes to its Ticket Captain, which claims it.

rules.rule: A captain-held Type goes to its Ticket Captain, which claims it.

units.text: For a map-holder-held Type, claim it before work; a Question still waits for the user's answer.

rules.rule: For a map-holder-held Type, claim it before work; a Question still waits for the user's answer.

units.text: Resolve a Wayfinding Ticket.
**Zoom as needed**: fetch the full body of any related or closed ticket on demand; use whichever methods the `## Notes` block names.

rules.rule: Zoom as needed: fetch the full body of any related or closed ticket on demand, using whichever methods the map's Notes block names.

units.text: Follow the ticket Type above.

rules.rule: Resolve the ticket following its Type's rules.

units.text: Record the resolution when the Type's outcome is reached: post the answer as a **resolution comment**, mark the ticket `Done`, and append a context pointer to the map's Resolutions so far.

rules.rule: When the Type's outcome is reached, post the answer as a resolution comment, mark the ticket `Done`, and append a context pointer to the map's Resolutions so far.

units.text: For local fog, link the resolution from the parent delivery ticket instead; the record is the whole report.

rules.rule: For local fog, link the resolution from the parent delivery ticket instead; the record is the whole report.

units.text: Add newly surfaced tickets (create then wire, a Project's Task into its Milestone); graduate any fog the answer has made specifiable, clearing each graduated patch from **Not yet specified** so it lives only as its new ticket.

rules.rule: Add newly surfaced tickets (create then wire, a Project's Task into its Milestone); graduate any fog the answer made specifiable, clearing each graduated patch from Not yet specified so it lives only as its new ticket.

units.text: If the answer reveals that a ticket sits beyond the destination, rule it out of scope.

rules.rule: If the answer reveals a ticket sits beyond the destination, rule it out of scope.

units.text: If the resolution invalidates other parts of the map, update or cancel those tickets.

rules.rule: If the resolution invalidates other parts of the map, update or cancel those tickets.

units.text: Other sessions may work unblocked tickets in parallel, so re-read Linear before every claim or map mutation.

rules.rule: Other sessions may work unblocked tickets in parallel, so re-read Linear before every claim or map mutation.

units.text: A call Balazs would otherwise be asked.
Use when an officer must decide one while he is away, prepare a DR-grade or irreversible one for him, or when he asks for it on any call.

rules.rule: Use what-would-balazs-do when an officer must decide a call while he is away, prepare a DR-grade or irreversible one for him, or when he asks for it on any call.

units.text: Make the call the way he would, or prepare it with the answer he would give.

rules.rule: Make the call the way he would, or prepare it with the answer he would give.

units.text: A tribunal of three tests it against his own words.

rules.rule: A tribunal of three tests the call against his own words.

units.text: From the repository root, read the Question Tickets and Communication and evidence sections of `dydo/reference/linear-workspace-standard.md`.

rules.rule: From the repository root, read the Question Tickets and Communication and evidence sections of `dydo/reference/linear-workspace-standard.md`.

units.text: From the repository root, read `dydo/project/decisions/_decisions.md`.

rules.rule: From the repository root, read `dydo/project/decisions/_decisions.md`.

units.text: A judge goes straight to the Tribunal section.

rules.rule: A judge goes straight to the Tribunal section.

units.text: Officers only, each inside its own remit: a captain on calls inside its ticket contract, the map holder on scope, destination, architecture and cross-ticket calls.

rules.rule: Only officers run the skill, each inside its own remit: a captain on calls inside its ticket contract, the map holder on scope, destination, architecture and cross-ticket calls.

units.text: Crew returns its call to its captain; the chief of staff never runs it.

rules.rule: Crew returns its call to its captain; the chief of staff never runs the skill.

units.text: A vote never widens an officer's remit.

rules.rule: A vote never widens an officer's remit.

units.text: Research first: a call the facts settle is no Question.

rules.rule: Research first: a call the facts settle is no Question.

units.text: DR-grade is the Decision Record test: hard to reverse, surprising without context, a real trade-off.
Away means `dydo mode show` reports `overnight` `on`; off or unreadable, he is present.

rules.rule: Away means `dydo mode show` reports `overnight` `on`; off or unreadable, he is present.

units.text: | Easily reversible | you decide; no skill | you decide; no skill |

rules.rule: An easily reversible call is decided by the officer without the skill, whether he is present or away.

units.text: | Above your say, below DR-grade | a plain Question; no skill | the tribunal decides; where his intent is unclear, the most reversible option, flagged |

rules.rule: A call above the officer's say but below DR-grade, while he is present, is a plain Question without the skill.
A call above the officer's say but below DR-grade, while he is away, is decided by the tribunal; where his intent is unclear, the most reversible option, flagged.

units.text: | DR-grade | the tribunal prepares the Question | the tribunal decides if unanimous, and writes the DR; that verdict is his approval |

rules.rule: A DR-grade call, while he is present, has the tribunal prepare the Question.
A DR-grade call, while he is away, is decided by the tribunal if unanimous, which writes the DR; that verdict is his approval.

units.text: | Irreversible | his alone; the tribunal prepares the Question | the same |

rules.rule: An irreversible call is his alone, present or away; the tribunal prepares the Question.

units.text: He may invoke this skill on any call.

rules.rule: He may invoke the skill on any call.

units.text: Invoked by him, it still follows this table, read in the away column: a reversible call is decided by the Verdict rules, and only an irreversible one, or one the tribunal cannot decide, waits for his word.

rules.rule: When he invokes the skill, it still follows the table in the away column: a reversible call is decided by the Verdict rules, and only an irreversible one, or one the tribunal cannot decide, waits for his word.

units.text: Only his own words are his precedent: Decision Records (superseded ones as history), the docs, his answered Questions and grillings, and past conversations where available.

rules.rule: Only his own words are his precedent: Decision Records (superseded ones as history), the docs, his answered Questions and grillings, and past conversations where available.

units.text: His Walkthrough verdicts, findings and skips are his own words too, and samples of his taste; a skip is a chunk he trusted without looking.

rules.rule: His Walkthrough verdicts, findings and skips are his own words too, and samples of his taste; a skip is a chunk he trusted without looking.

units.text: A later word outranks an earlier one.

rules.rule: A later word of his outranks an earlier one.

units.text: A tribunal's output is never precedent until he ratifies it.

rules.rule: A tribunal's output is never precedent until he ratifies it.

units.text: Search the current project unless he points it at another project's records.

rules.rule: Search the current project for precedent unless he points it at another project's records.

units.text: Case law is evidence of his intent, not a rulebook.

rules.rule: Case law is evidence of his intent, not a rulebook.

units.text: Read why he decided, from the DRs, the core docs such as `dydo/guides/coding-standards.md`, the project's stated purpose and common sense, and decide in that spirit, with or without a precedent.

rules.rule: Read why he decided, from the DRs, the core docs such as `dydo/guides/coding-standards.md`, the project's stated purpose and common sense, and decide in that spirit, with or without a precedent.

units.text: A recorded decision that goes against that spirit or no longer fits the project loses to it: the position names the decision and why, and the call becomes DR-grade, or at least flagged.

rules.rule: A recorded decision that goes against his spirit or no longer fits the project loses to it: the position names the decision and why, and the call becomes DR-grade, or at least flagged.

units.text: A citation quotes his words with the reason behind them.

rules.rule: A citation quotes his words with the reason behind them.

units.text: Run it by [tribunal](resources/tribunal.md); judges load this skill and follow the same file.

rules.rule: Run the tribunal by `resources/tribunal.md`; judges load this skill and follow the same file.

units.text: Each member's ballot names one exact, written action.

rules.rule: Each tribunal member's ballot names one exact, written action.

units.text: | DR-grade | all three naming the same text | no decision: a prepared Question |

rules.rule: For a DR-grade call, a decision needs all three members naming the same text; otherwise no decision, a prepared Question.

units.text: | below DR-grade | two naming the same text | three different actions: the most reversible option, flagged |

rules.rule: For a call below DR-grade, a decision needs two members naming the same text; with three different actions, the most reversible option, flagged.

units.text: While he is present and has not invoked it, the result is always a prepared Question carrying the predicted answer and any dissent.

rules.rule: While he is present and has not invoked the skill, the result is always a prepared Question carrying the predicted answer and any dissent.

units.text: An incomplete tribunal decides nothing; the call becomes a prepared Question.

rules.rule: An incomplete tribunal decides nothing; the call becomes a prepared Question.

units.text: Every call the tribunal takes is a `Question` ticket in `Todo`, his turn, with the tribunal log attached as a Linear Document.

rules.rule: Every call the tribunal takes is a `Question` ticket in `Todo`, his turn, with the tribunal log attached as a Linear Document.

units.text: A call you decide without the skill needs no record here.

rules.rule: A call decided without the skill needs no record here.

units.text: **Decided:** post `DECIDED - by: what-would-balazs-do tribunal, unratified; result: <action>; vote: <n of 3, or split; most reversible>; log: <link>; undo: <steps>; next: <action>.` Leave the Question unwired; work resumes, and any review the work requires still runs.

rules.rule: When decided, post `DECIDED - by: what-would-balazs-do tribunal, unratified; result: <action>; vote: <n of 3, or split; most reversible>; log: <link>; undo: <steps>; next: <action>.`, leave the Question unwired, and let work resume with any required review still running.

units.text: A DR-grade decision also writes the repo DR `status: proposed`, `ratification: pending`, linking the log.

rules.rule: A DR-grade decision also writes the repo DR with `status: proposed` and `ratification: pending`, linking the log.

units.text: **Prepared or not decided:** no `DECIDED` post.

rules.rule: When prepared or not decided, post no `DECIDED`.

units.text: The Question's body carries the prediction, any dissent, the stop reason and the log link; wire it as a blocker of every waiter.

rules.rule: The prepared Question's body carries the prediction, any dissent, the stop reason and the log link, and is wired as a blocker of every waiter.

units.text: **His answer:** post `RATIFIED` or `OVERTURNED` in the standard's form, quoting him, and move the Question to `Done`.

rules.rule: On his answer, post `RATIFIED` or `OVERTURNED` in the standard's form, quoting him, and move the Question to `Done`.

units.text: Ratified, the DR becomes `accepted`.

rules.rule: When ratified, the DR becomes `accepted`.

units.text: Overturned, the DR becomes `deprecated`, or `superseded` by the record his answer calls for, quotes his answer, and the affected work reopens.

rules.rule: When overturned, the DR becomes `deprecated`, or `superseded` by the record his answer calls for, quotes his answer, and the affected work reopens.

units.text: Either way, drop `ratification`.

rules.rule: Either way, drop `ratification` from the DR.

units.text: Three members, Popper-style: each position stands only while it survives the strongest challenge.

rules.rule: Tribunal has three members, each position standing only while it survives the strongest challenge.

units.text: The raising officer is a full member and also the clerk.

rules.rule: The raising officer is a full tribunal member and also the clerk.

units.text: The clerk is mechanical: it forwards text verbatim, tracks turns and claims, and tallies ballots; its view enters only through its own turns.

rules.rule: The clerk is mechanical: it forwards text verbatim, tracks turns and claims, and tallies ballots; its view enters only through its own turns.

units.text: Set every phase's deadline when you open the case file.

rules.rule: Set every tribunal phase's deadline when you open the case file.

units.text: Append each finished phase to the log before the next.

rules.rule: Append each finished phase to the log before the next.

units.text: **Case file.**
Research the case law, sending `research` sparingly where a source is out of reach.

rules.rule: Research the case law, sending `research` sparingly where a source is out of reach.

units.text: Write the case file below.

rules.rule: Write the case file in the given form.

units.text: Done when it holds every option, unranked.

rules.rule: The case-file phase is done when it holds every option, unranked.

units.text: **Seal.**
Write and log your own sealed position before any judge starts.

rules.rule: Write and log your own sealed position before any judge starts.

units.text: **Dispatch.**
Start two fresh judges as T3 `delegate_task` children, one Claude and one Codex, each with the strongest model and effort set explicitly.

rules.rule: Start two fresh judges as T3 `delegate_task` children, one Claude and one Codex, each with the strongest model and effort set explicitly.

units.text: Send each the judge brief with the case file.

rules.rule: Send each judge the judge brief with the case file.

units.text: Done when both return sealed positions and their results show the model and effort asked for.

rules.rule: The dispatch phase is done when both judges return sealed positions and their results show the model and effort asked for.

units.text: **Rounds.**
Send every member the same bundle: the sealed positions and the last round's turns, always queued, never steered.

rules.rule: Each round, send every member the same bundle: the sealed positions and the last round's turns, always queued, never steered.

units.text: Write your own turn before reading theirs.

rules.rule: Write your own turn before reading theirs.

units.text: Each turn raises the strongest material objection to another member's position, or says why none exists, and answers the strongest outstanding challenge to its own.

rules.rule: Each turn raises the strongest material objection to another member's position, or says why none exists, and answers the strongest outstanding challenge to its own.

units.text: A concession quotes the evidence or restates the argument it yields to.

rules.rule: A concession quotes the evidence or restates the argument it yields to.

units.text: **Claims.**
A factual claim names its check; the other two members run it independently and report confirmed, refuted or inconclusive.

rules.rule: A factual claim names its check; the other two members run it independently and report confirmed, refuted or inconclusive.

units.text: A reframe states exactly what it changes, and the judges may object.

rules.rule: A reframe states exactly what it changes, and the judges may object.

units.text: No class is lowered over an unresolved objection: the strictest class stands.

rules.rule: No class is lowered over an unresolved objection: the strictest class stands.

units.text: **Close.**
Stop when a round changes nothing and no claim is pending, and after 4 rounds at most, evidence rounds and reframes included.

rules.rule: Stop the rounds when a round changes nothing and no claim is pending, and after 4 rounds at most, evidence rounds and reframes included.

units.text: **Ballot.**
List every option still standing, each as one exact action quoted from the final positions.

rules.rule: The ballot lists every option still standing, each as one exact action quoted from the final positions.

units.text: Each member names one of them, verbatim.

rules.rule: Each member names one ballot option, verbatim.

units.text: Tally by the verdict table in the skill.

rules.rule: Tally the ballot by the verdict table in the skill.

units.text: A missing or stalled member gets one retry.

rules.rule: A missing or stalled member gets one retry.

units.text: After that the tribunal is incomplete and ends without a decision; never swap a vendor silently.

rules.rule: After the retry the tribunal is incomplete and ends without a decision; never swap a vendor silently.

units.text: An experiment goes to a proof-only `code-writer` in an isolated worktree, its effects contained; its brief names the commissioning captain, the pinned source SHA and the test path.

rules.rule: An experiment goes to a proof-only `code-writer` in an isolated worktree, its effects contained; its brief names the commissioning captain, the pinned source SHA and the test path.

units.text: Members otherwise only read.

rules.rule: Tribunal members otherwise only read.

units.text: Judges get this and nothing else from your session:

rules.rule: Judges get the judge brief and nothing else from the raising officer's session.

units.text: the call, in one sentence; the objective; the constraints
the options, unranked
the primary evidence, quoted with its source and why he decided: stated by him, or inferred and naming the DRs or docs it rests on
each premise, stated as a claim with its source
your class for the call, and whether he is present or away
the member's own class for the call

rules.rule: A sealed position has this form: the member's own class, the call in its own words, an option the file did not list or why none exists, the premises checked and what it found, its answer with any recorded decision it overrides, and what would change its mind.

units.text: the call, in its own words
an option the file did not list, or why none exists
the premises it checked, and what it found
its answer: the action he would take and why, naming any recorded decision it overrides
what would change its mind
You are a judge on a `what-would-balazs-do` tribunal.

rules.rule: A judge brief tells the judge it is a judge on a `what-would-balazs-do` tribunal.

units.text: Load that skill and follow its `resources/tribunal.md`.

rules.rule: A judge loads the `what-would-balazs-do` skill and follows its `resources/tribunal.md`.

units.text: Answer as Balazs would, in the spirit of his words, citing why he decided.

rules.rule: A judge answers as Balazs would, in the spirit of his words, citing why he decided.

units.text: You may send `research` subagents after evidence.

rules.rule: A judge may send `research` subagents after evidence.

units.text: Return your sealed position in the skill's form by <deadline>.

rules.rule: A judge returns its sealed position in the skill's form by the brief's deadline.

units.text: Later rounds arrive as queued messages; answer each with one turn.

rules.rule: Later rounds arrive to a judge as queued messages; it answers each with one turn.

units.text: As a judge, use the Sealed position form and phases 4-7 as a member; phases 1-3, the clerk duties and writing the ballot list are the clerk's.

rules.rule: As a judge, use the Sealed position form and phases 4-7 as a member; phases 1-3, the clerk duties and writing the ballot list are the clerk's.

units.text: Never dispatch judges.

rules.rule: A judge never dispatches judges.

units.text: Case file: <case file>

notRule.note: judge brief template slot for the case file

units.text: A Linear Document `Tribunal log - <KEY>`, attached to the Question.

rules.rule: Keep the tribunal log as a Linear Document `Tribunal log - <KEY>`, attached to the Question.

units.text: Checkpoint `Dispatch` on every dispatch and retry, and append each round once complete, so a fresh clerk resumes without dispatching a judge twice or resetting a retry.

rules.rule: Checkpoint `Dispatch` on every dispatch and retry, and append each round once complete, so a fresh clerk resumes without dispatching a judge twice or resetting a retry.

units.text:
```markdown
## Case file
## Dispatch
<member>: task <id>; deadline <time>; retries <n>; pending: <turn or none>
## Sealed positions
<member> - <role/model and effort, as the result shows them>: <position>
## Round <n>
<member>: <turn, verbatim>
## Claims
<claim> | <check> | <member>: confirmed, refuted or inconclusive
## Ballot
<option, exact text>
<member>: <option, exact text>
## Verdict
result: <decision, prepared Question, or no decision>; stop: converged, cap or incomplete; undo: <steps>
```

rules.rule: The tribunal log has this form: Case file, Dispatch, Sealed positions, Round n, Claims, Ballot, Verdict.
